knowledge:
- key_parameters: orgdb=The organism database package name (e.g., "org.Hs.eg.db") used to fetch GO term sizes and calculate semantic similarity ;; ont=The Gene Ontology of interest, which must be one of "BP" (Biological Process), "MF" (Molecular Function), or "CC" (Cellular Compartment) ;; method=The semantic similarity measure from GOSemSim (e.g., "Rel", "Resnik", "Lin", "Jiang", "Wang") ;; semdata=An optional pre-calculated GOSemSim::godata object to speed up repeated runs for the same organism and ontology ;; scores=An optional named vector of scores associated with each GO term (e.g., -log10(qvalue)); higher scores are favored ;; threshold=Similarity threshold (0 to 1) used for grouping terms; higher thresholds lead to fewer groups (minimum similarity between group representatives)
- alternatives: REVIGO=A web tool that rrvgo mimics in core functionality; use rrvgo for a programmatic R/Bioconductor interface ;; GOStats or GSEA=Methods/packages to identify the initial enriched GO terms before using rrvgo ;; AnnotationForge=Used to build custom OrgDb objects if the organism is not supported by Bioconductor
- when_to_use: When you have a list of enriched GO terms (e.g., from a differential expression analysis) that is redundant, long, and difficult to interpret, and you want to group them into representative functional themes and visualize them.
- pitfalls: Scores are interpreted in the direction that higher is better; if using p-values or q-values as scores, they must be minus log-transformed (e.g., -log10(qvalue)) before passing to reduceSimMatrix ;; If semdata is not pre-calculated and saved, running calculateSimMatrix multiple times for the same organism will be slow because it calculates it on demand.

workflows.name: reduce_and_visualize_go_redundancy
workflows.intent: Reduce redundancy in a list of enriched Gene Ontology (GO) terms using semantic similarity and visualize the grouped terms.
input: go_analysis.txt (a tab-delimited text file containing GO term IDs and q-values/scores)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate the semantic similarity matrix using calculateSimMatrix ;; 2. Transform q-values to scores and reduce the similarity matrix using reduceSimMatrix ;; 3. Visualize the reduced terms using heatmapPlot, scatterPlot, treemapPlot, and wordcloudPlot
workflows.code:
library(rrvgo)
go_analysis <- read.delim(system.file("extdata/example.txt", package="rrvgo"))
simMatrix <- calculateSimMatrix(go_analysis$ID,
                                orgdb="org.Hs.eg.db",
                                ont="BP",
                                method="Rel")
scores <- setNames(-log10(go_analysis$qvalue), go_analysis$ID)
reducedTerms <- reduceSimMatrix(simMatrix,
                                scores,
                                threshold=0.7,
                                orgdb="org.Hs.eg.db")
heatmapPlot(simMatrix,
            reducedTerms,
            annotateParent=TRUE,
            annotationLabel="parentTerm",
            fontsize=6)
scatterPlot(simMatrix, reducedTerms)
treemapPlot(reducedTerms)
wordcloudPlot(reducedTerms, min.freq=1, colors="black")
